publishedExpectations.claim: SIG states its business 'thrives at the intersection of trading, quantitative research, and technology' and that candidates will be 'continuously challenged to solve some of the most complex problems in the financial markets'.
SIG builds 'the fastest and most powerful trading systems in the industry by combining infinite data sources and sophisticated coding with innovative engineering and problem solving'.
Student and grad roles combine 'challenging, hands-on work with classroom education', with a unique learning plan per group that builds on existing skills.
The careers page's 'Who We Are' section is titled 'Game Theory + Decision Science', signalling the firm's decision-science framing of its work.

notes: SIG's official careers pages confirm the three core disciplines (trading, technology, quantitative research + ML), the performance-and-stability framing of its systems work, and structured classroom education for new hires. The firm self-brands around game theory and decision science, which matches its public identity but is not an interview-format claim. Community-reported patterns (unverified): a multi-week training 'bootcamp' in the Bala Cynwyd area, probability/game-theory heavy interviews with expected-value and game questions, and mental-math screens for trading; no retrieved official page confirms these details. Interview round counts and test names should be treated as unconfirmed.
